𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐛𝐫𝐨𝐜𝐚𝐬 𝐚𝐫𝐞𝐬 𝐢𝐬 𝐚𝐟𝐟𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐞𝐝 ?\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E• Broca's area is located in the frontal lobe of the brain, specifically in the left hemisphere. It's situated in the posterior part of the frontal gyrus, which is responsible for speech production and language processing. It is supplied by the middle cerebral artery. So in MCA infarct it can affect this brocas area and can lead to difficulty in speech\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E2. 𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐬𝐞𝐧𝐬𝐨𝐫𝐲 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐦𝐨𝐭𝐨𝐫 𝐚𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐬 𝐬𝐮𝐩𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐞𝐝 𝐛𝐲 𝐌𝐂𝐀 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐰𝐡𝐢𝐜𝐡 𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐚𝐟𝐟𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐢𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E• The middle cerebral artery (MCA) primarily supplies blood to various regions of the cerebral cortex. Sensory and motor areas supplied by the MCA include parts of the face, upper and lower limbs, and areas involved in sensory and motor functions. The specific regions can vary among individuals, but generally, the MCA contributes to the blood supply of the lateral convexity of the cerebral hemisphere. This includes the precentral gyrus (primary motor cortex) and the postcentral gyrus (primary somatosensory cortex). Damage to the MCA can lead to motor and sensory deficits on the contralateral side of the body.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E3. 𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐢𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐫𝐨𝐥𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐚𝐬𝐩𝐢𝐫𝐢𝐧 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐜𝐥𝐨𝐩𝐢𝐝𝐨𝐠𝐫𝐞𝐥 𝐢𝐧 𝐜𝐞𝐫𝐞𝐛𝐫𝐨𝐯𝐚𝐬𝐜𝐮𝐥𝐚𝐫 𝐚𝐜𝐜𝐢𝐝𝐞𝐧𝐭?\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E• Aspirin and clopidogrel are antiplatelet medications commonly used in the management of cerebrovascular accidents (CVAs), also known as strokes. They help prevent blood clot formation by inhibiting platelet aggregation, which is crucial in reducing the risk of further vascular events.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\"Aspirin\" works by blocking the action of an enzyme called cyclooxygenase, thereby inhibiting the production of thromboxane A2, a substance that promotes platelet aggregation. Clopidogrel, on the other hand, is a platelet inhibitor that blocks the activation of platelets by preventing specific receptors from binding.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E4. 𝐑𝐨𝐥𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐝𝐮𝐚𝐥 𝐚𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐩𝐥𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐥𝐞𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐩𝐲 𝐢𝐧 𝐜𝐞𝐫𝐞𝐛𝐫𝐨𝐯𝐚𝐬𝐜𝐮𝐥𝐚𝐫 𝐚𝐜𝐜𝐢𝐝𝐞𝐧𝐭?\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E• Dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) involves the use of two antiplatelet medications concurrently, commonly aspirin and clopidogrel, to further reduce the risk of recurrent cerebrovascular accidents (CVAs). The rationale behind DAPT is to enhance the antiplatelet effect and inhibit different pathways involved in platelet activation and aggregation.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E• The combination of aspirin and clopidogrel is often prescribed after certain types of ischemic strokes or transient ischemic attacks (TIAs). This approach is particularly relevant in cases of acute coronary syndrome or high-risk conditions, where the benefit of preventing blood clot formation outweighs the potential risks associated with dual therapy.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E• The duration of dual antiplatelet therapy is also carefully determined based on the specific circumstances of each patient.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E5. 𝐑𝐨𝐥𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐬 𝐢𝐧 𝐂𝐕𝐀?\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E• Statins play a significant role in the management of cerebrovascular accidents (CVAs), particularly ischemic strokes. Ischemic strokes are often caused by atherosclerosis, a condition characterized by the buildup of cholesterol and fatty deposits in the arteries supplying blood to the brain. Statins are a class of medications that primarily target cholesterol levels in the blood.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E𝐋𝐄𝐀𝐑𝐍𝐈𝐍𝐆 𝐏𝐎𝐈𝐍𝐓𝐒 :-\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E• I learnt the Importance of proper history taking as it may show up with many differential diagnosis and confirming one from them .\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E• Importance of early diagnosis\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAs in this case due to their delay the situation got worsen. So early treatment is important.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E•\u0026nbsp; I learnt how much is it important to educate patients family members to look after their geriatric patient and not neglecting any of her condition\u0026nbsp; thereafter.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E• I learnt about the dosage of the medications and their side effects.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E"},"link":[{"rel":"edit","type":"application/atom+xml","href":"https:\/\/www.blogger.com\/feeds\/2689134584147960837\/posts\/default\/6446935204952436971"},{"rel":"self","type":"application/atom+xml","href":"https:\/\/www.blogger.com\/feeds\/2689134584147960837\/posts\/default\/6446935204952436971"},{"rel":"alternate","type":"text/html","href":"https:\/\/alekya19.blogspot.com\/2023\/12\/osce-prefinal-examination.html","title":"OSCE PREFINAL EXAMINATION "}],"author":[{"name":{"$t":"Alekya Kallem"},"uri":{"$t":"http:\/\/www.blogger.com\/profile\/11305056354282255364"},"email":{"$t":"noreply@blogger.com"},"gd$image":{"rel":"http://schemas.google.com/g/2005#thumbnail","width":"16","height":"16","src":"https:\/\/img1.blogblog.com\/img\/b16-rounded.gif"}}]},{"id":{"$t":"tag:blogger.com,1999:blog-2689134584147960837.post-8972428966252444774"},"published":{"$t":"2023-12-05T20:21:00.000-08:00"},"updated":{"$t":"2023-12-05T21:06:42.585-08:00"},"title":{"type":"text","$t":"65 yr old female cva case"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cdiv\u003EThis is an online e log book to discuss our patient de-identified health data shared after taking his \/ her \/ guardians signed informed consent. Here we discuss our individual patients problems through series of inputs from available global online community of experts with an aim to solve those patients clinical problem with collective current best evident based input.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThis E blog also reflects my patient centered online learning portfolio and your valuable inputs on the comment box is welcome.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EI have been given this case to solve in an attempt to understand the topic of \" patient clinical data analysis\" to develop my competency in reading and comprehending clinical data including history, clinical findings, investigations and come up with diagnosis and treatment plan.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPatient and his\/her attenders have been informed and their consent has been taken.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EA 65 yr old female was brought to the casualty with\u0026nbsp; complaints of\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E• Difficulty in moving upper limbs and lower limbs since 3 days\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E• Unable to speak since 3 days\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E𝐇𝐈𝐒𝐓𝐎𝐑𝐘 𝐎𝐅 𝐏𝐑𝐄𝐒𝐄𝐍𝐓𝐈𝐍𝐆 𝐈𝐋𝐋𝐍𝐄𝐒𝐒:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPatient was apparantly assymptomatic 3 days back, then she developed weakness in left upper and lower limbs ( on Saturday afternoon )which was sudden in onset , gradually progressed first appeared in the upper limb and then in the lower limb associated with slurred speech and was trying to convey something. On Sunday afternoon weakness developed into left sided hemiplegia developed and complete loss of speech occured\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E• No H\/O
